concept.name: Execution error
concept.definition: A mistake in implementing an intended trade - wrong order type or price, fat-fingered size, missed or late entry, early or late exit relative to plan - as distinct from a flawed idea. It is measured as the gap between intended and actual execution.
concept.intuition: The analysis was right and the plan was right; the fingers or the timing were wrong.
concept.mechanics: Detected by comparing each trade to its plan: slippage versus expected fill, entry timing versus trigger, exit versus exit rule. Sources include inattention, platform errors, latency, and emotional hesitation; mitigations are checklists, hotkeys with size limits, and rehearsed order routines.
concept.failure_modes: Execution errors are most frequent exactly when markets are fastest and stakes highest; in leveraged instruments a single size or order-type error can exceed all planned risk. They are undercounted unless intent is recorded before the trade.
concept.misconceptions: A profitable fat-finger is still an error, not a win; grading by outcome hides the defect. Small repeated execution leaks (late entries, chasing fills) compound into a large expectancy drag even when each instance seems trivial.
concept.example: Intending a limit buy at 50.00 with a 49.50 stop, a trader market-buys at 50.35 in a spike; the extra 0.35 of slippage turns a planned 2:1 trade into 1.4:1 before it starts.
